title: Seasons
examples: Why does the angle of the sun change throughout the year?
How does the tilt of the Earth affect the seasons?
Is the change in day length the main reason for seasons?

explain.say: The Earth is tilted on its axis as it travels around the Sun.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: Earth's tilt and the seasons. Look at the sun, the tilted axis and the june. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
This tilt means that different parts of Earth get more sunlight at different times.
During the summer, a hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun receiving more direct light.
This tilt also changes the number of daylight hours we experience throughout the year.
In the winter, a hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun getting less direct light.
In real life, imagine the change in day length when you move north or south.

faq.q: Does the Earth change its tilt over time?
faq.a: No, the Earth's axial tilt remains relatively constant over short periods. This tilt is what causes the seasons. You might ask: What keeps the tilt steady? Or: Is the tilt permanent?

faq.q: Is the distance from the Sun the main cause of seasons?
faq.a: No, the distance is not the main cause of seasons. The tilt of the Earth relative to the Sun is the primary reason. You might ask: Does Earth get closer to the Sun in summer? Or: Does distance matter more than tilt?
At the equinoxes, the day and night are almost equal in length everywhere on Earth. This happens twice a year. You might ask: What is an equinox? Or: Are the days equal at this time?

faq.q: Why is the summer in the Northern Hemisphere?
faq.a: The Northern Hemisphere experiences summer when it is tilted towards the Sun. This means it receives more direct sunlight. You might ask: Which way is the tilt for summer? Or: Why is it summer here?
asks: How do I know it is summer?

faq.q: What is the difference between solstice and equinox?
faq.a: The solstices mark the longest and shortest days, while the equinoxes mark the equal days. The solstices happen when the tilt is at its extreme. You might ask: Which is longer, solstice or equinox? Or: What do these words mean?
asks: What are the extremes of the year?

facts: The Earth's axis is tilted at an angle of approximately twenty-three point five degrees.
The seasons are caused by this axial tilt, not by the Earth's changing distance from the Sun.
During the summer solstice, the day length is at its maximum for that hemisphere.
The equinoxes mark the times when day and night are nearly equal in length everywhere.

quiz.say: The seasons are mainly caused by:

options.show: The Earth getting closer to the Sun in summer.
options.say: The Earth getting closer to the Sun in summer.

options.show: The Sun changing its power output.
options.say: The Sun changing its power output.

options.show: The Earth's speed in its orbit.
options.say: The Earth's speed in its orbit.

options.show: The tilt of the Earth's axis.
options.say: The tilt of the Earth's axis.

quiz.why: The tilt means different hemispheres get varying amounts of direct sunlight.

wrong.0: This is tempting because we feel warmer, but the distance change is not the main cause.
wrong.1: This is a common misconception, but the Sun's energy output is stable enough.
wrong.2: Speed changes are not the factor that dictates seasonal changes.

quiz.say: When is the day length at its shortest?
quiz.why: The winter solstice marks the point when a hemisphere is tilted furthest from the Sun.

wrong.0: At the equinox, the day and night are nearly equal, not the shortest.
wrong.1: The summer solstice is when the day length is at its maximum.
wrong.2: Day length changes gradually, so mid-year is not a specific point.

quiz.say: If a hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, what season is it experiencing?
quiz.why: Tilting towards the Sun means the region receives more direct and longer daylight hours.

wrong.0: Spring is a transition period, not the peak of direct sunlight.
wrong.2: Winter occurs when the hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun's energy.
wrong.3: An equinox means the day and night are balanced, not that one is dominant.
